page0.text:
"Urgh."
The pain where Assassin punched me in the stomach brings me back to my senses.
...Rider and I are the only ones left in the shrine room.
I take a deep breath to calm myself down.
After a moment,
I realize that only my stomach and back are hurting.

page1.text:
"Sa..."
I know what that means now, even without thinking about it.

page2.text:
"...ber..."
I push through my dizziness and head for the corridor.

page3.text:
"Wait. It's dangerous to go alone."
"You..."
Rider doesn't seem to mean me any harm.
She was really here to save me.

page4.text:
"Why did you..."
Save me, I almost finish, but I almost don't care at this point.
Right now, I want to...

page5.text:
"You're Shinji's Servant. Why would you help me?"
I want to go to her.
Why am I taking this detour?

page6.text: "I was commanded not to let you die. I simply followed my Master's orders."

page7.text:
...I see.
Whatever. I don't believe it, but if that's her answer, then fine.
Never mind that. I need...to hurry...

page8.text:
"..."
...
I know with one glance what I'm going to find.

page9.text:
The corridor is silent.
It's half-destroyed, torn apart as if a tornado went through.
On the only intact portion of the floor, I find a red stain.

page10.text:
It's smaller than the palm of my hand, and I don't know who the blood belongs to.
But as soon as I see it, I feel my legs go weak, and I drop to my knees.

page11.text:
...
I touch the red stain.
The blood is dry, and it doesn't stick to my fingers.
It seems to declare that she's well and truly gone.

page12.text: "My duty is to protect you, Shirou."

page13.text:
...
How many times have I heard those words?
They were promising, yet anxious.
...She always put me first.
Never once did she talk about protecting herself.

page14.text:
...
I scratch at the blood stain.
Saber fought and died here.
That's what war is.
I've known from the moment we made our pact that people would die in this battle.
I offered her my hand with that in mind, and she took it.

page15.text:
"Saber..."
She was a girl smaller than me, who protected me.
When I decided to go after the black Shadow instead of the Holy Grail, she swallowed her dread and went along with my decision.

page16.text:
...And this is the result.
I lost her, I'm no longer a Master, and I'm back to being the half-baked "hero" I was before.
I'm all alone, with no way to fight.
But I still have something to do.

page17.text:
"I need to go."
I touch the blood stain one last time.
This is farewell.
I lift my hand away, without a bow or word of thanks.

page18.text:
The pain in my left hand is gone.
The moment I acknowledged Saber's death and said goodbye,
my Command Spells disappeared without a trace.

page19.text:
...Command Spells won't disappear just because a Servant is gone.
They go away when a mage is no longer qualified to be a Master.

page20.text:
"Oh. So I..."
I have no idea what happened here tonight.
All I know for certain is one thing:
In this moment, I lost Saber and the right to be a Master.

page21.text:
...I leave Ryudou Temple.
My stomach and back feel like big injuries, but right now, I don't care about physical discomfort.

page22.text:
"I will escort you home. It's dangerous to walk alone at night, even if the enemy is gone."
"...Huh?"
I stop, surprised.
The way Rider is acting is just too unexpected.

page23.text:
"I don't get it. Did your Master order that, too?"
"No, I've received no such order. I am acting on my personal feelings. I simply thought it was the best thing to do."

page24.text:
"...All right. I can believe that, but I'll pass on the escort. We're enemies. You don't need to go out of your way for me."
"Enemies... Do you still intend to fight me, then? You, not even a mage and without Saber?"

page25.text:
...
I don't answer.
I still haven't said anything about fighting or forfeiting the war.

page26.text:
"I see. Very well, then. Take care on the way home."
Rider's long hair flutters.
She heads for the mountain gate ahead of me.
Even to me, she looks hopelessly defenseless from behind.

page27.text:
"...Thanks."
I blurt out something I forgot to say.

page28.text:
"Huh?"
She turns around, surprise plain on her face.
"Ugh..."
It's embarrassing to have her look at me like that, but I have to express my gratitude.

page29.text:
"What did you just say?"
...Because she'll hear me, after all.
I feel uncomfortable staring her in the eye, so I slightly avert my gaze.

page30.text:
"I-I said thank you. I would've died if you didn't save me.
...As you can see, I have nothing to pay you back with. So it wouldn't be right unless I thanked you."

page31.text:
"You need not concern yourself with it. I only followed my Master's orders.
Those same orders could change and tell me to kill you on a moment's notice."
Rider answers in a cold voice, and disappears through the gate.

page32.text: "Yeah. That's why I told you not to go out of your way."
